name: Salt Lake (Bidhannagar)
description: Salt Lake, or Bidhannagar as it is officially called, sits in North 24 Parganas and has grown into Kolkata's technology powerhouse. Its Sector V IT Park, widely regarded as eastern India's biggest tech cluster, is where software majors like TCS and Wipro, plus Cognizant, Infosys and Capgemini, keep their offices. The township was planned from scratch, so you get wide roads and neatly ordered sectors that make driving around surprisingly easy. Between Nicco Park and Central Park, together with the Nalban Food Park, there is plenty to see, and the Kolkata Book Fair sets up each year at Milan Mela Prangan. For anyone commuting to the airport or the office, a cab is the most dependable way to get around.

name: New Town (Rajarhat)
description: Rajarhat, better known to most people simply as New Town, is the fastest-expanding satellite township in Kolkata today. The modern, planned layout with its broad avenues has attracted scores of IT parks and residential complexes, and global firms such as Wipro, HCL and Accenture now call it their Kolkata base. Within the township, Eco Park ranks among India's largest urban parks, while the Biswa Bangla Convention Centre hosts exhibitions and conferences throughout the year. Passengers heading to the airport find it especially convenient, since the terminals lie just 8 km away, and the TCS campus alongside the upcoming Kolkata Eye hospital keeps the demand for rides steady at all hours.

name: Howrah
description: Howrah sits directly opposite Kolkata on the far bank of the Hooghly, and the two cities are linked by the celebrated Howrah Bridge, officially Rabindra Setu. Crossing it every day, lakhs of passengers pour in and out of Howrah Junction, one of the oldest and busiest railway stations in the country. The district also holds a few genuine treasures: the Botanical Garden and its centuries-old Great Banyan Tree, the Belur Math headquarters of the Ramakrishna Mission, and the wide expanse of Howrah Maidan. Because so many train journeys begin or end here, arriving or departing visitors lean on local cabs to bridge the final stretch between the station and the airport 22 km away.

name: Park Street
description: Park Street, whose official name is Mother Teresa Sarani, has long been the city's stage for nightlife and culture. Its pavements are lined with colonial-era buildings, heritage eateries like Flurys, Peter Cat, Mocambo, plus Trincas, and shops that fill up after sundown, earning it the nickname of Kolkata's Food Street. Around the corner sit the Maidan, Victoria Memorial, St. Paul's Cathedral and the Indian Museum, so sightseeing and fine dining can easily be combined into a single evening. Visitors staying in the hotels nearby usually book a car for airport transfers, since the journey covers roughly 16 km of central city traffic.

name: Dum Dum (Airport Area)
description: Dum Dum, tucked in North Kolkata, is a name every air traveller in the region quickly comes to recognise, for it is home to Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose International Airport. The locality's history runs deep — the Dum Dum Arsenal, an ammunition works from the British era, is said to be where the name itself originated. These days the area operates as a busy interchange, with Metro, buses and autos fanning out across the city from its corners. Since the airport sits barely 2 km away, most passengers arriving by flight depend on cabs to carry them onward, and pre-booked cars are the standard choice to avoid last-minute waits.

name: Ballygunge
description: Ballygunge ranks among the most desirable addresses in South Kolkata, prized for its tree-shaded avenues, heritage facades and quiet proximity to the Maidan. Families are drawn here partly by the cluster of reputed colleges nearby, including St. Xavier's, Loreto and Presidency University, and partly by the easy commute this neighbourhood offers. The Rabindra Sadan and Jatin Das Park metro stations put the rest of the city within reach, while Quest Mall, Forum Mall, and the famous Gariahat Market take care of everything from groceries to designer shopping. For residents travelling out, the airport is about 18 km down the road, a trip most make comfortably in a booked cab rather than on public transport.

name: Tollygunge
description: Locals affectionately shorten it to 'Tolly', a corner of South Kolkata that pairs a rich past with comfortable modern living. This is where the Bengali film industry, better known as Tollywood, first made its name, and the lawns of the Tollygunge Club still carry that old-world charm. Around the neighbourhood you will also find Rabindra Sarobar, the largest lake-park in the city, the historic Tollygunge Racecourse, and Nalban Park. Being right on the Metro corridor keeps commuting simple, while a ride to the airport runs about 20 km — short enough that most households simply hail a cab when heading out of town.

name: Barasat
description: Barasat is a substantial suburban hub that doubles as the administrative capital of North 24 Parganas district, sitting roughly 25 km north of Kolkata's centre. Its position on Jessore Road (NH12) and on BT Road makes it the natural jumping-off point for the Sundarbans, Basirhat and much of the northern belt. The town itself is in the middle of a building boom, with fresh residential projects and commercial complexes springing up steadily. Travellers use it frequently as both a pickup and drop point, and with the airport only 15 km away, cab operators are a common sight on its highways.

name: Behala
description: Behala is a crowded, hardworking residential stretch in the southwest of Kolkata, anchored around the busy Behala Chowrasta junction. Diamond Harbour Road, together with James Long Sarani, carry its traffic toward the centre of the city, while the Joka Metro line runs along one edge and the Behala Flying Club gives the area its own distinctive landmark. Apartment blocks, schools and local markets have multiplied here over the years as the neighbourhood grew into a full-fledged suburb. For residents heading out on longer trips, a cab is close to essential: public transport to the airport and the main railway stations is thin, and the 25 km run to the airport is best covered door-to-door.

name: Esplanade (BBD Bagh)
description: Esplanade and its neighbour BBD Bagh, the old Dalhousie Square, together form the historic core where Kolkata's government and business life is conducted. The Writers' Building, the Kolkata High Court, the General Post Office, and the Reserve Bank of India all sit within this compact district. It is also the city's great transport clearing house, with the Esplanade bus terminus — the largest in Kolkata — despatching services to suburban and outstation destinations alike. Between delegations of business travellers, visitors on government work and tourists tracing the city's colonial past, the area keeps cab drivers moving through most of the day, with the airport roughly 17 km away.

name: Gariahat
description: Gariahat is the kind of neighbourhood South Kolkata revolves around, equally important for its shopping and its homes. The Gariahat crossing and its famous market never seem to rest, with clothing stalls, handicraft sellers and street-food vendors working side by side. Buses, trams and autos all thread through the area, while South City Mall and Golpark, with Dhakuria Lake and Lake Mall close at hand, offer a change of pace. Families and professionals who work across the southern parts of the city tend to settle here, and a 19 km drive to the airport in a booked cab is the way most residents prefer to travel out.

name: Jadavpur
description: Jadavpur carries a distinctly youthful energy, thanks above all to Jadavpur University, among the most respected seats of learning in India. Around its campus the neighbourhood blends academic buildings with homes, small businesses and a lively strip of cafes and bookshops that the students keep buzzing. The 8B Bus Stand operates as a key interchange, moving people from south Kolkata to every other part of the city, with autos filling the gaps and a Metro extension still on the way. It is a dependable pickup point for taxi operators too, especially since the airport lies about 20 km up the road.
